I always find myself consulting documentation to remember how to configure tools, so this is a compiled reference of [pre-commit](https://pre-commit.com) hooks I use most.

::: {.callout-tip}
If you not familiar with pre-commit, check the previous article:
[Git hooks and pre-commit](./../2024-04-18-git-hooks-and-pre-commit/).
:::

Each section contains hooks for a language, or a set of languages.
The first code block always shows the repository and hook mappings in the _.pre-commit-config.yaml_ file.
A baseline for configuration of the hook or tool is also given.
Refer to the linked documentations for fine-tuning to your needs.

As sometimes rules do not apply or they are false positives, every code linter has a way to ignore rules.
Usually it can be done in the command line, in the configuration file, or in code itself.
These options are illustrated in each section, when applicable.

## General

pre-commit has its own set of hooks that are quite generic and can be used in any project.
Details about each hook can be found in the [_pre-commit-hooks_ repository](https://github.com/pre-commit/pre-commit-hooks?tab=readme-ov-file#hooks-available).

```yaml
repos:
  - repo: https://github.com/pre-commit/pre-commit-hooks
    rev: v3.2.0
    hooks:
      - id: check-added-large-files
      - id: check-merge-conflict
      - id: check-toml
      - id: end-of-file-fixer
      - id: requirements-txt-fixer
      - id: trailing-whitespace
```

## Python

### uv

[Astral.sh](https://github.com/astral-sh) is coming up with several promising tools for the Python ecosystem.
I highly recommend checking out [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/), a project and package manager.

_uv_ uses a lock file to ensure that all developers in a project are using the same versions of dependencies.
While `uv add <package>` automatically updates the lock file, if you edit `pyproject.toml` manually, you may forget to update the lock file.

The `uv-lock` hook checks if the lock file is up to date with the `pyproject.toml` file and prevents commits if it is not.

```yaml
repos:
  - repo: https://github.com/astral-sh/uv-pre-commit
    rev: 0.11.3
    hooks:
      - id: uv-lock
```

### ruff

Ruff, also from Astral.sh, really impressed me as an all-in-one code formatter and linter for Python.
It wraps a lot of tools and extensions in a single place and is faster than _Flake8_ or _PycodeStyle_.

:::{.callout-tip}
Ruff also has an [extension for VS Code](https://marketplace.visualstudio.com/items?itemName=charliermarsh.ruff).
:::

```yaml
repos:
  # Format/lint: Python
  - repo: https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff-pre-commit
    rev: v0.15.9
    hooks:
      - id: ruff-check
        args: [--fix]
      - id: ruff-format
```

Ruff can be configured through a _pyproject.toml_, _ruff.toml_, or _.ruff.toml_ file.
See [Configuring Ruff](https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/configuration/) for the default configuration
and [Settings](https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/settings/) for a comprehensive list of configuration options.

```toml
# pyproject.toml

[tool.ruff]
target-version = "py310"

[tool.ruff.lint]
extend-select = [
  "I",    # isort
  "A",    # flake8-builtins
  "B",    # flake8-bugbear
  "SIM",  # flake8-simplify
]
```

The [inline ignore syntax](https://flake8.pycqa.org/en/3.1.1/user/ignoring-errors.html#in-line-ignoring-errors)
is:

```python
#> Ignore rule F841
i = 0  # noqa: F841

#> Ignore rules multiple rules
j = 1  # noqa: E741, F841

#> Ignore _all_ violations
k = 2  # noqa
```

The syntax applies to `flake8` (see below).

### black + flake8 + isort

> I highly recommend using [Ruff](#ruff) instead of these because it wraps so much in
> a single tool (and configuration file).

The canonical code formatter and linter tools for Python.

- `black`: code formatter
- `flake8`: code linter
- `isort`: sort Python imports

```yaml
repos:
  # Format: Python
  - repo: https://github.com/psf/black
    rev: 24.4.2
    hooks:
      - id: black

  # Lint: Python
  - repo: https://github.com/PyCQA/flake8
    rev: 7.0.0
    hooks:
      - id: flake8

  # Format: Python imports
  - repo: https://github.com/PyCQA/isort
    rev: 5.13.2
    hooks:
      - id: isort
```

Configuration is more troublesome, because you have to look for options in a bunch of different documentations and may be a lot of tweaking between tools.
That is why I am enjoying Ruff so much.
For reference, here is a sample configuration:

```toml
# pyproject.toml

[tool.black]
target-version = ["py310"]
line-length = 88

[tool.isort]
profile = "black"
line_length = 88
multi_line_output = 3
include_trailing_comma = true
virtual_env = "venv"
```

```ini
# .flake8 (flake8 does not support pyproject.toml)

[flake8]
extend-ignore =
  "E501",  # Line too long
  "W503",  # Line break occurred before binary operator
  "E226",  # Missing white space around arithmetic operator
```

## R

Code lint and formatting are powered by [`lintr`](https://lintr.r-lib.org/index.html)
and [`styler`](https://styler.r-lib.org/index.html), respectively.

```yaml
repos:
  # Format/lint: R
  - repo: https://github.com/lorenzwalthert/precommit
    rev: v0.4.2
    hooks:
      - id: lintr
        name: Lint R
      - id: style-files
        name: Format R
      - id: no-print-statement
        name: Check print statement
```

The repository includes [other useful hooks](https://github.com/lorenzwalthert/precommit/blob/main/.pre-commit-hooks.yaml)
directed at packages like `roxygen2` and `pkgdown`.

You may configure `lintr` with the _.lintr_ file.
See [Configuring linters](https://lintr.r-lib.org/articles/lintr.html#configuring-linters)
and [Available linters](https://lintr.r-lib.org/reference/linters.html)
for more configuration options.

```R
# .lintr

linters: linters_with_defaults(
    line_length_linter(88),
    commented_code_linter = NULL
  )
```

The [inline ignore syntax](https://styler.r-lib.org/articles/styler.html#ignoring-certain-lines) is:

- Ignore current line:

  ```R
  #> Ignore line
  ignore( this) # styler: off
  f( ) # not ignored anymore
  ```

- Ignore code block:

  ```R
  foo <- 0

  # styler: off
  I_have(good+reasons, to = turn_off,
  styler
  )
  # styler: on

  bar <- 1
  ```

## SQL

[SQLFluff](https://docs.sqlfluff.com/en/stable/) is a code linter and formatter for several dialects of SQL.
It helps detecting bad practices and _inneficiencies_ in your query, besides auto-formatting your code.
Great tool for refactoring prototype or legacy code.

```yaml
repos:
  - repo: https://github.com/sqlfluff/sqlfluff
    rev: stable_version
    hooks:
      - id: sqlfluff-lint
        args: [--dialect, postgres]
      - id: sqlfluff-fix
        args: [--dialect, postgres]
```

SQLFluff support several [configuration files](https://docs.sqlfluff.com/en/stable/configuration.html#configuration-files),
such as _.sqlfluff_ and _pyproject.toml_.
Check the [Default Configuration](https://docs.sqlfluff.com/en/stable/configuration.html#default-configuration)
and [Rule index](https://docs.sqlfluff.com/en/stable/rules.html#rule-index) for full reference.

```toml
# pyproject.toml

[tool.sqlfluff.core]
templater = "jinja"
sql_file_exts = ".sql,.sql.j2,.sql.jinja2"

[tool.sqlfluff.indentation]
indented_joins = false
indented_using_on = true
template_blocks_indent = false

[tool.sqlfluff.templater]
unwrap_wrapped_queries = true

[tool.sqlfluff.templater.jinja]
apply_dbt_builtins = false

# For rule specific configuration, use dots between the names exactly
# as you would in .sqlfluff. In the background, SQLFluff will unpack the
# configuration paths accordingly.
[tool.sqlfluff.rules.capitalisation.keywords]
capitalisation_policy = "upper"
```

The [inline ignore syntax](https://docs.sqlfluff.com/en/stable/rules.html#inline-ignoring-errors) is:

- Ignore current line:

  ```sql
  -- Ignore one or more rules
  SELECT
    a.a*a.b AS bad_1,  -- noqa: LT01
    a.a *  a.b AS bad_2,  -- noqa: LT01, LT03
  FROM my_table
  ```

- Ignore code block:

  ```sql
  -- Ignore rule AL02 from this line forward
  SELECT col_a a FROM foo -- noqa: disable=AL02

  -- Ignore all rules from this line forward
  SELECT col_a a FROM foo -- noqa: disable=all

  -- Enforce all rules from this line forward
  SELECT col_a a FROM foo -- noqa: enable=all
  ```

## YAML, JSON, Markdown

[Prettier](https://prettier.io/docs/en/) is a code formatter devoted to front-end languages like
JavaScript, TypeScript, HTML and many more, but it also has plugins for other languages.
As you may be using only a subset of its supported languages,
limiting which files Prettier will run on can improve performance.

Prettier is a good choice for YAML, JSON and Markdown files.
In the configuration below, I only select files with extension _.ymal_, _.yml_, _.json_, and _.md_.

```yaml
repos:
  # Format: YAML, JSON and Markdown
  - repo: https://github.com/pre-commit/mirrors-prettier
    rev: v4.0.0-alpha.8
    hooks:
      - id: prettier
        files: ^(.*\.ya?ml|.*\.json|.*\.md)$
```

There are several configuration files names, I will use `.prettierrc.yaml` here.
See [Configuration file](https://prettier.io/docs/en/configuration) for more options.

```yaml
# .prettierrc.yaml

tabWidth: 2
endOfLine: lf
```

## YAML

In addition to [Prettier](#webdev-yaml-json-and-more),
[`yamllint`](https://yamllint.readthedocs.io/en/stable/) provides a code linter for YAML files.

```yaml
repos:
  # Lint: YAML
  - repo: https://github.com/adrienverge/yamllint
    rev: v1.35.1
    hooks:
      - id: yamllint
        args: ["-d {extends: relaxed, rules: {line-length: disable}}", "-s"]
        files: \.(yaml|yml)$
```

The [inline ignore syntax](https://yamllint.readthedocs.io/en/stable/disable_with_comments.html) is:

- Disable one or more rules in a line:

  ```yaml
  # yamllint disable-line rule:line-length
  disable-rule: This line is waaaaaaaaaay too long but yamllint will not report anything about it

  # yamllint disable-line rule:hyphens rule:commas
  disable-rules: [hyphens, commas]

  # yamllint disable-line
  disable-all: Disable _all_ rules (not recommended)
  ```

- Disable one or more rules in a code block:

  ```yaml
  disable-rules:
      # yamllint disable rule:colons
      - Lorem       : ipsum
      dolor       : sit amet,
      consectetur : adipiscing elit
      # yamllint enable rule:colons

  disable-all:
      # yamllint disable
      - Lorem       :
              ipsum:
              dolor : [   sit,amet]
      -         consectetur : adipiscing elit
      # yamllint enable
  ```

## Markdown

In addition to [Prettier](#webdev-yaml-json-and-more),
[`markdownlint-cli`](https://github.com/igorshubovych/markdownlint-cli)
provides a code linter for Markdown files.

```yaml
repos:
  # Lint: Markdown
  - repo: https://github.com/igorshubovych/markdownlint-cli
    rev: v0.40.0
    hooks:
      - id: markdownlint
        args: ["--fix"]
```

Configuration can be set in a `.markdownlint.yaml` file.
The configuration below addresses a common issue with tables:
it lets them be as long as they need to.
See [Rules](https://github.com/DavidAnson/markdownlint/blob/main/doc/Rules.md)
for a description of all rules.

```yaml
# .markdownlint.yaml

# Default state for all rules
default: true

# MD013/line-length - Line length
MD013:
  line_length: 100
  tables: false
```

The [inline ignore syntax](https://github.com/DavidAnson/markdownlint/tree/main?tab=readme-ov-file#configuration)
is:

```markdown
Disable one or more rules for the current line. <!-- markdownlint-disable-line MD001 MD005 -->

<!-- markdownlint-disable MD001 MD005 -->

Disable/enable one or more rules in a block.

- MD001: heading-increment

* MD005: list-indent

<!-- markdownlint-enable MD001 MD005 -->

<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

Disable/enable _all_ rules in a block.

<!-- markdownlint-enable -->
```

## Shell and Bash

Shell and bash scripts are pretty common in many projects.

- `shellcheck-py`: builds on top of [ShellCheck](https://github.com/koalaman/shellcheck),
  a shell script linter.
  Rules for ShellCheck can be found in the [Wiki pages](https://www.shellcheck.net/wiki/)
- `bashate`: a linter for bash scripts, complementing ShellCheck.
  See rules in [Currently Supported Checks](https://github.com/openstack/bashate?tab=readme-ov-file#currently-supported-checks).

```yaml
repos:
  # Lint: Shell scripts
  - repo: https://github.com/shellcheck-py/shellcheck-py
    rev: v0.10.0.1
    hooks:
      - id: shellcheck
        args: ["-x"]

    # Lint: Bash scripts
  - repo: https://github.com/openstack/bashate
    rev: 2.1.1
    hooks:
      - id: bashate
```

ShellCheck may be configured in the `.shellcheckrc` file.

```sh
# .shellcheckrc

# Don't suggest [ -n "$VAR" ] over [ ! -z "$VAR" ]
disable=SC2236

# Suggest ${VAR} in place of $VAR
enable=require-variable-braces
```

The [inline ignore syntax](https://www.shellcheck.net/wiki/Ignore) is:

- Disable one or more rules in a line:

  ```sh
  #!/bin/sh

  source $(dirname "$0/utils.sh")

  # shellcheck disable=SC2059,SC2034
  echo "Disable rules SC2059 and SC2034 for this line"

  # shellcheck disable=all
  echo "Disable all rules for this line"
  ```

- Disable all rules in a file:

  ```sh
  #!/bin/sh
  # shellcheck disable=SC2059,SC2034

  source $(dirname "$0/utils.sh")

  echo "Disable rules SC2059 and SC2034 in the entire file."
  echo "Must be at the top of the file"
  ```

## Docker

Hadolint helps a lot in improving the stability of Docker images as well as reducing their overall size.

```yaml
repos:
  # Lint: Dockerfile
  - repo: https://github.com/hadolint/hadolint
    rev: v2.12.0
    hooks:
      - id: hadolint
```

Configuration may be done in a `.hadolint.yaml` file.
You can find the list of [Rules](https://github.com/hadolint/hadolint?tab=readme-ov-file#rules)
in the repository.

```yaml
# .hadolint.yaml

ignored:
  - DL3008 # Pin versions in `apt-get install`
```

The [inline ignore syntax](https://github.com/hadolint/hadolint?tab=readme-ov-file#ignoring-rules) is:

- Ignore one or more rules in a file:

```Dockerfile
# hadolint global ignore=DL3003,DL3006,SC1035
FROM ubuntu:22.04

RUN echo "global"
```

- Ignore one or more rules in a line:

```Dockerfile
# hadolint ignore=DL3006
FROM ubuntu

# hadolint ignore=DL3003,SC1035
RUN echo "line"
```
